newsitem.title: TANZANIA: EU signs $211 million aid deal with Tanzania.
newsitem.headline: EU signs $211 million aid deal with Tanzania.

text.p: The European Union said on Tuesday it had signed an agreement to give Tanzania 240.5 million Ecus ($211 million) in aid over the next five years.
It was the second largest aid deal given to a state in the African, Caribbean and Pacific group of developing countries and the largest EU aid package for Tanzania, officials said.
Half of the money would go to the transport sector, said Athanassios Theodorakis, deputy director-general of the European Commission for Development and Cooperation.

"In a country the size of Tanzania with its population and natural resources spread throughout the country it is vital to have modern, efficient and effective domestic and international transport services," he said.
The balance would go to water, education, poverty alleviation, environment and women's programmes.
With a per capita income of around $160, Tanzania is one of the world's poorest countries and its inadequate road network is a major reason why it lags behind East African neighbours.
Tanzania must maintain EU-funded infrastructure improvements, said Theodorakis, calling for the establishment of a road fund.
Donors have threatened to withold funding for road projects after Tanzania failed to contribute its 10 percent share of costs to a donor-funded roads project launched in 1991.
The money was supposed to have been raised from fuel and transport levies.
EU assistance to Tanzania totals more than $1.3 billion over 20 years, said senior treasury official Peter Ngumbullu.
"The government is gradually moving out of a largely managed and owned public economy and is encouraging wider participation of the private sector instead," he said.
